distance_decay_exponent.definition: fitted n in |sigma_A - 1| = C (d/L)^(-n) (informative, not gated)

distance_decay_far_field_kd_gated.definition: max |sigma_A_heave - 1| over the points with k d >= 4.0 (k d is the physically relevant far-field parameter: the radiated wave decays like (k r)^-1/2, so d/L alone cannot gate it)

energy_non_negative_damping.definition: min over configurations, modes and resolved frequencies of B_mm

geometry.definition: finest-mesh displaced volume vs analytic Cb*L*B*T

infinite_frequency_added_mass_catamaran.definition: same comparison for the two-hull configuration

infinite_frequency_added_mass_catamaran_.definition: same 1/omega^2 fit for the pair, restricted to resolved ladder rows outside the detected resonance bands

infinite_frequency_from_kramers_kronig.definition: |A(inf) from the Kramers-Kronig moment of the measured B - A_pressure_release| / A_pressure_release, worst mode

infinite_frequency_from_kramers_kronig_d.definition: A(inf) = A(0) - (2/pi) int B/w^2 dw over the resolved ladder (A(0) Richardson-extrapolated; tail carried by a B ~ w^-p fit)

negative_control_singularity.definition: gap -> 0 raises the interference and superposed hulls break the system

resonance_bands.definition: narrow-band resonances: B_mm local maximum >= 2.0 x the mean of its two neighbours in the fine scan delta(omega/omega_n)=0.025 (informative: recorded, not gated)

zero_frequency_added_mass_extrapolated.definition: Richardson-extrapolated (p=2) A(0) vs the same extrapolation of the omega_min radiation row

zero_frequency_added_mass_fine.definition: |A(omega_min) - A_rigid_wall| / A_rigid_wall on a matched refinement mesh at omega/omega_n = 0.1 (the scan's lowest frequency); worst mode

zero_frequency_added_mass_limit.definition: the same comparison at omega/omega_n = 0.02, where the O(omega^2) correction is small enough for the omega -> 0 limit to be measured (the trend is recorded separately)

zero_frequency_damping.definition: max_m [ B_m(omega_min) / max_omega B_m ] over the resolved sweep (each mode normalised by its own peak)
